questions.question: After masking and softmax, what must be true of the permitted attention weights for one query and one head?
options: They sum to one within floating-point tolerance.
They each equal the sequence length.
They are copied directly from the value vectors.
They are always uniform across permitted tokens.
questions.explanation: Softmax normalizes the permitted query-key scores into a probability-like weighting whose values sum to one.

questions.question: Why does an autoregressive decoder apply a causal mask during next-token training?
options: To reduce the vocabulary to one token.
To prevent each position from using future target tokens as input evidence.
To let every position read the complete target sequence.
To remove the need for position information.
questions.explanation: Future tokens are the labels the decoder is learning to predict. Revealing them through attention would leak the answer.

questions.question: What is the purpose of dividing query-key dot products by the square root of the key dimension?
options: It deletes masked positions from the tokenizer.
It changes a decoder into an encoder.
It keeps score magnitudes from making softmax excessively sharp as the dimension grows.
It guarantees every attention head learns the same pattern.
questions.explanation: The scaling controls dot-product magnitude, helping keep softmax in a range with useful gradients.

questions.question: Which architecture has causal self-attention in the target stack and a separate cross-attention path to encoded source representations?
options: Encoder-only
Feed-forward-only
Decoder-only with no source
Encoder-decoder
questions.explanation: An encoder-decoder model first represents the source, then lets the causal decoder cross-attend to those source representations.

questions.question: A decoder has 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, an 8,192-token cache, and 2-byte cache elements. Approximately how much KV cache does one sequence require?
options: 1 GiB
8 MiB
16 GiB
32 GiB
questions.explanation: 2 x 32 x 8,192 x 8 x 128 x 2 bytes equals 1,073,741,824 bytes, or 1 GiB.

questions.question: Why is changing a serving configuration from MHA to GQA not usually a free runtime toggle?
options: GQA removes all query projections from the model.
The checkpoint's key and value projections must match the grouped-query architecture or be deliberately converted and evaluated.
GQA can run only on CPUs.
The tokenizer determines the number of KV heads.
questions.explanation: KV-head count is part of the learned model shape. Compatible weights or a measured conversion process are required.

questions.question: What does FlashAttention primarily change for exact full attention?
options: It changes the model from causal to bidirectional.
It removes all pairwise query-key arithmetic.
It tiles the computation to reduce expensive memory reads and writes without approximating the attention result.
It stores one KV head for every vocabulary token.
questions.explanation: FlashAttention is IO-aware: it reduces data movement and avoids materializing the full attention matrix in high-bandwidth memory while computing exact attention.
